brief: C++ interface to Zymkey Application Utilities Library.
intro:
This file contains the C++ API to the the Zymkey Application Utilities library, `libzkAppUtilsClassCPP`. Systems intending to run such applications require that the `libzkapputils-c++` package be installed.

This class facilitates writing user space applications which use Zymkey to perform cryptographic operations, such as:

1. Signing of payloads using ECDSA
1. Verification of payloads that were signed using Zymkey
1. Exporting the public key that matches Zymkey's private key
1. "Locking" and "unlocking" data objects
1. Generating random data Additionally, there are functions for changing the I2C address (I2C units only), setting tap sensitivity and controlling the LED.

Developers wishing to build applications which utilize the `libzkAppUtilsClassCPP` library should additionally install the `libzkapputils-c++-dev` package, which contains the necessary development files for the Zymkey's C++ library. To install this package on a system that does not need to run the applications (e.g. a Docker container or when cross compiling on another architecture), use `apt install --no-install-recommends libzkapputils-c++-dev`. This will prevent `apt` from installing the Zymkey's `zkifc` driver daemon.

Usage:

```
#include <zymkey/zkAppUtilsClass.h>
```

To add `libzkAppUtilsClassCPP` as a dependency of a CMake-based project, add the following lines to your project's `CMakeLists.txt`:

```
find_package(zkAppUtilsCXX REQUIRED)
target_link_libraries(${target_name} zkAppUtilsCXX::zkAppUtilsClassCPP)
```

Statically linking to the library is also supported within CMake by way of the `zkAppUtilsCXX::zkAppUtilsClassCPP_static` library target.

Projects may alternatively import the library dependency via `pkg-config`:

```
CFLAGS="$(pkg-config --cflags zkapputils-c++)"
LDFLAGS="$(pkg-config --libs zkapputils-c++)" 
```

params.name: chain_code
params.description: (output) Allocated chain_code if it was asked for.

returns.description: Allocated slot number if successful, less than 0 for failure.

items.name: restoreWalletMasterSeedFromMnemonic
items.signature: int zkAppUtils::zkClass::restoreWalletMasterSeedFromMnemonic(ZK_EC_KEY_TYPE type, std::string &wallet_name, byteArray &master_generator_key, recoveryStrategyBIP39 &recovery_strategy, std::string &mnemonic_str)
items.brief: Restore a master seed from a BIP39 mnemonic and a master generator key.
items.details: This function restores a wallet master seed from a supplied BIP39 mnemonic string and a master generator key.

params.name: type
params.description: The type of key to generate (ZK_KEY_TYPE). {ZK_NISTP256, ZK_SECP256R1 = ZK_NISTP256, ZK_SECP256K1}

params.name: wallet_name
params.description: An ASCII string which contains the name of the wallet.

params.name: master_generator_key
params.description: The master generator key used to help generate the master seed.

params.name: recovery_strategy
params.description: The recovery strategy used. Contains the passphrases and key variant to recover from.

params.name: mnemonic_str
params.description: The mnemonic sentence to recover the master seed with. (Not used for SLIP39)

returns.description: Allocated slot number if successful, less than 0 for failure.

items.name: restoreWalletMasterSeedFromMnemonic
items.brief: Start a SLIP39 session to restore a master seed.
items.details: The shards are then fed in with addRestoreSLIP39Mnemonic.

params.name: type
params.description: The type of key to restore (ZK_EC_KEY_TYPE).

params.name: wallet_name
params.description: An ASCII string which contains the name of the wallet.

params.name: master_generator_key
params.description: The master generator key used to help generate the master seed.

params.name: recovery_strategy
params.description: The SLIP39 passphrase and key variant to recover from.

returns.description: The result of opening the session; less than 0 for failure.

items.name: addRestoreSLIP39Mnemonic
items.brief: Feed a SLIP39 shard to restore a master seed.
items.details: This function will feed a shard to the module until the conditions are met and a master seed is generated.

params.name: passphrase
params.description: The passphrase that was attached to the shard.

params.name: mnemonic_sentence
params.description: (output) The twenty-four word sentence mnemonic shard.

returns.description: allocated slot number when all shards required are fed in, less than 0 for no change.

items.name: getWalletNodeAddrFromKeySlot
items.brief: Derive the node address from a key slot number.
items.details: This function derives a node address from an input key slot number.

params.name: slot
params.description: (input) A key slot number that is part of a digital wallet.

params.name: out_node_addr
params.description: (output) A pointer to a string which will contain the node address in ASCII.

params.name: out_wallet_name
params.description: (output) A pointer to a string which will contain the wallet name in ASCII. If NULL, this parameter will not be retrieved.

returns.description: The master seed key slot.

items.name: getWalletKeySlotFromNodeAddr
items.brief: Derive the slot address from a node address.
items.details: This function returns the slot number associated with a given node address.

params.name: node_addr
params.description: (input) A pointer which contains the node address in ASCII.

params.name: wallet_name
params.description: (input) A pointer which contains the wallet name in ASCII, used to identify the wallet identity. If desired, this parameter can be NULL and the master_seed_slot parameter can be specified instead.

params.name: master_seed_slot
params.description: (input) The master seed slot. Can be used to specify the wallet identity instead of the wallet name.

returns.description: The associated key slot.

items.name: setI2CAddr
items.brief: Sets the i2c address (i2c versions only). Used in case of i2c bus device address conflict.

params.name: addr
params.description: The i2c address to set. Upon successful change, the Zymkey will reset itself. However, if the address is the same as the current setting, the Zymkey will not reset. Valid address ranges are 0x30 - 0x37 and 0x60 - 0x67.

items.name: getTime
items.brief: Get current GMT time.
items.details: This method is called to get the time directly from a Zymkey's Real Time Clock (RTC)

params.name: precise_time
params.description: (input) If true, this API returns the time after the next second falls. This means that the caller could be blocked up to one second. If false, the API returns immediately with the current time reading.

returns.description: The time in seconds from the epoch (Jan. 1, 1970).

items.name: setPerimeterEventAction
items.brief: Set perimeter breach action.
items.details:
This function specifies the action to take when a perimeter breach event occurs. The possible actions are any combination of:

- Notify host
- Zymkey self-destruct

params.name: channel
params.description: (input) The channel (0 or 1) that the action flags will be applied to.

params.name: action_flags
params.description:
(input) The actions to apply to the perimeter event channel:

- Notify (ZK_PERIMETER_EVENT_ACTION_NOTIFY)
- Self-destruct (ZK_PERIMETER_EVENT_ACTION_SELF_DESTRUCT)

items.details: This function sets low power period on the digital perimeter detect

params.name: lp_period
params.description: (input) low power period in microseconds

returns.description: void.

items.name: setDigitalPerimeterDetectLPMaxBits
items.brief: Set the low power max number of bits.
items.details: This function sets low power max number of bits on the digital perimeter detect

params.name: max_num_bits
params.description: (input) max number of bits

returns.description: void.

items.name: setDigitalPerimeterDetectDelays
items.brief: Set the delays.
items.details: This function sets delays on the digital perimeter detect

params.name: min_delay_ns
params.description: (input) minimum delay in nanoseconds

params.name: max_delay_ns
params.description: (input) maximum delay in nanoseconds

returns.description: void.

items.name: waitForPerimeterEvent
items.brief: Wait for a perimeter breach event to be detected.
items.details: This function is called in order to wait for a perimeter breach event to occur. This function blocks the calling thread unless called with a timeout of zero. Note that, in order to receive perimeter events, the zymkey must have been configured to notify the host on either or both of the perimeter detect channels via a call to "zkSetPerimeterEventAction".

params.name: timeout_ms
params.description: (input) The maximum amount of time in milliseconds to wait for a perimeter event to arrive.

items.name: getPerimeterDetectInfo
items.brief: Get current perimeter detect info.
items.details: This function gets the timestamp of the first perimeter detect event for the given channel

params.name: timestamp_sec
params.description: (output) The timestamps for when any events occurred. The index in this array corresponds to the channel number used by zkSetPerimeterEventAction. A 0 value means no breach has occurred on this channel. This array is allocated by this routine and so it must be freed by the caller.

params.name: num_timestamps
params.description: (output) The number of timestamps in the returned array

items.brief: Get the CPU Temp.
items.details: This function gets the current HSM CPU temp.

returns.description: The CPU temp as a float.

items.name: getAUXTemp
items.brief: Get the AUX Temp. (Secure Compute Modules Only)
items.details: This function gets the current temp of an aux processor. (defaults to 0). THIS FUNCTION IS FOR INTERNAL ZYMBIT USE ONLY.

returns.description: The CPU temp as a float.

items.name: getRTCDrift

items.details: This function gets the current RTC drift.

returns.description: The RTC drift as a float.

items.name: getBatteryVoltage
items.brief: Get the battery voltage.
items.details: This function gets the current battery voltage

returns.description: the battery voltage as a float.

items.name: setBatteryVoltageAction
items.brief: Set battery voltage threshold action.
items.details:
This function specifies the action to take when the battery voltage falls below the threshold set by zkSetBatteryVoltageThreshold. If this function is never called, do nothing is default. There are three actions:

- Do nothing
- Go to sleep until battery is replaced
- Self-destruct

params.name: action
params.description:
(input) The action to apply, specify one of the ZK_THRESHOLD_ACTION_TYPE:

- Do nothing (ZK_ACTION_NONE)
- Sleep (ZK_ACTION_SLEEP)
- Self-destruct (ZK_ACTION_SELF_DESTRUCT)

items.name: setBatteryVoltageThreshold
items.brief: Sets the battery voltage threshold.
items.details: This function sets the threshold at which if the battery voltage falls bellow, the action set by zkSetBatteryVoltageAction will be carried out. The recommended threshold is 2.3V is assumed by default. Threshold must be below 2.5V.

params.name: threshold
params.description: (input) The threshold in Volts.

items.name: setCPUTempAction
items.brief: Set HSM CPU temperature threshold action.
items.details:
This function specifies the action to take when the HSM CPU temperature falls below the threshold set by zkSetCPULowTempThreshold, or rises above the threshold set by zkSetCPUHighTempThreshold. There are two actions to apply:

- Do nothing
- Self-destruct

params.name: action
params.description:
(input) The action to apply, used it's named constant from ZK_THRESHOLD_ACTION_TYPE:

- Do nothing (ZK_ACTION_NONE)
- Self-destruct (ZK_ACTION_SELF_DESTRUCT)

items.name: setCPULowTempThreshold
items.brief: Sets the HSM CPU low temperature threshold.
items.details: This function sets the threshold at which if the on-board HSM CPU's tempreature falls below, the action set by zkSetCPUTempAction will be carried out. WARNING: You can lock yourself out in dev mode if you set a threshold above the CPU's ambient temperature. The recommended setting is no more than 20C. If no threshold is set, -10 degrees Celsius is set as default.

params.name: threshold
params.description: (input) The threshold in celsius.

items.name: setCPUHighTempThreshold
items.brief: Sets the HSM CPU high temperature threshold.
items.details: This function sets the threshold at which if the on-board HSM CPU's tempreature rises above, the action set by zkSetCPUTempAction will be carried out. WARNING: You can lock yourself out in dev mode if you set a threshold below the CPU's ambient temperature. The recommended setting is no less than 40C. If no threshold is set, 65 degrees celsius is set as default.

params.name: threshold
params.description: (input) The threshold in celsius.

returns.description: 0 for success, less than 0 for failure.

items.name: setSupervisedBootPolicy
items.brief: Sets the Supervised boot policy.
items.details: This function specifies the action to take when Supervised boot event triggers based on a file change.

params.name: policy_id
params.description:
(input) The actions to apply to the Supervised boot process:

- 0 Do Nothing (ZK_SUPBOOT_FAIL_NO_ACTION)
- 1 Self-Destruct (ZK_SUPBOOT_FAIL_DESTROY)
- 2 Hold Chip in Reset (ZK_SUPBOOT_FAIL_HOLD_RESET)

returns.description: 0 for success, less than 0 for failure.

returns.description: 0 for success, less than 0 for failure.

returns.description: 0 for success, less than 0 for failure.
